lines.en: Colin, you look so happy! What happened this morning?
lines.pt: Colin, você parece tão feliz! O que aconteceu esta manhã?

lines.en: **You won’t believe it.** **I was playing** my fiddle in the park **when** a man stopped to listen.
lines.pt: Você não vai acreditar. Eu estava tocando meu violino no parque quando um homem parou para ouvir.

lines.en: **While** I was playing, he took out his phone and started recording. **Suddenly** he said, “Can you play that again?”
lines.pt: Enquanto eu tocava, ele pegou o celular e começou a gravar. De repente disse: “Você pode tocar isso de novo?”

lines.en: Wait, what? What was he doing in the park?
lines.pt: Peraí, o quê? O que ele estava fazendo no parque?

lines.en: He was walking his dog. He’s a radio producer, and he was looking for a street musician.
lines.pt: Ele estava passeando com o cachorro. Ele é produtor de rádio e estava procurando um músico de rua.

lines.en: That’s incredible! So how did it end?
**In the end,** he gave me his card and invited me to play on his radio show!
lines.pt: No fim, ele me deu o cartão e me convidou para tocar no programa de rádio dele!

lines.en: Congratulations! I knew it was going to be a good day for you.
lines.pt: Parabéns! Eu sabia que seria um bom dia para você.

pages.title: Telling stories (past continuous)

situation.text: Something surprising happened to you this morning. In the park, you tell a friend the story: what you were doing, what happened and how it ended.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can tell a short story with a beginning, a surprise and an ending, using was/were + -ing and linking words.
canDo: Set the scene: I was… when…
Use while for two actions at the same time
Use Suddenly / Then / In the end
React to a story: And then what happened?
success: I react to my partner’s story.
pages.think: Think of a small surprising thing that happened to you recently. What were you doing at that moment?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação: contar o que aconteceu de forma organizada.
solo: Peça ao estudante um momento surpreendente recente.
Mostre os 4 critérios.
group: Cada estudante diz o que estava fazendo ontem às 8 da noite.
Anote no quadro.
extra: What is the best story you tell at parties?
Who tells the best stories in your family?
support: Aceite respostas curtas e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Ask about the student’s week; listen for the past simple and recycle travel experiences.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: Experiences (class 88): “Have you ever…?” and “I’ve never…”. Ask: What is something you have never done?

qs.q: Did anything funny happen this week?
Who tells the best stories in your family?

pages.tip: Use the first question to hear was/were + -ing naturally, without naming the grammar.

teach.goal: Ativar passado e criar contexto para histórias.
extra: What were you doing when you got my message?
What were you doing last Sunday afternoon?

errors.w: I was go to the park.
errors.r: I went to the park. / I was going to the park.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Story structure
pages.intro: Good stories follow a simple pattern that English speakers recognize. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: When, where, what you were doing: “I was walking in the park…”
“Suddenly…” or “Then…” brings the event that changes everything.
“Really?”, “No way!”, “And then what happened?” keep the story alive.

qs.q: Why is “Suddenly” useful in a story?
qs.pt: Por que “Suddenly” é útil numa história?

levels.A2: It shows a surprise: something changed quickly.
levels.B1: It marks the turning point after the background description.
levels.B2: It signals a sudden event in the narrative and creates a moment of suspense.

qs.q: What do listeners do while you tell a story?
qs.pt: O que os ouvintes fazem enquanto você conta?

levels.A2: They say “Really?” or “No way!” and ask questions.
levels.B1: They react and ask follow-ups, such as “And then what happened?”
levels.B2: They use short reactions and questions to show they are following and invite more detail.

levels.A2: With “In the end…” and how you felt.
levels.B1: With the result and a short comment about how you felt or what you learned.
levels.B2: With the outcome and a brief reflection, often with a light or humorous comment.

pages.compare: In Brazil, people also love telling stories and listeners interrupt with “nossa!” and “e aí?”. In English, short reactions like “Really?” and “And then?” do the same job. Which reactions do you use?

teach.goal: Mostrar a estrutura de uma boa história e as reações do ouvinte.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com “nossa!” e “e aí?”.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica.
Pergunte “Do you agree?”.
extra: What reactions do you use in Portuguese?
Do you like long or short stories?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: conte a mesma história em 3 frases e em 8.

pass1.pt: O que o Colin está fazendo?
opts: Telling a story about his morning

teach.goal: Entender a história e depois 5 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: ideia principal.
2ª escuta: lugar, instrumento, cachorro, profissão e convite.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Mostre o texto só no final.
answers: Pass 1: a story about his morning.
Pass 2: park · fiddle · dog · radio producer · radio show.
extra: How does Vera react?
Is Colin lucky? Why?
support: Use “Slow” e pause após cada fala.

qs.q: What was Colin doing when the man stopped?
What did the man do while Colin was playing?
Why was the man in the park?
opts: He was walking his dog and looking for a musician
The man invited him to a radio show

retell.prompt: Retell the story in your own words.
starters: While he was playing, the man…

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar com a estrutura da história.
solo: O estudante lê Colin; você lê Vera.
Reconto com os conectores.
group: Leitura em duplas.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante, cada uma começando com um conector.
answers: Playing his fiddle · He recorded him · walking his dog and looking for a musician · invited to a radio show
extra: What would you do in Colin’s place?
What was Vera doing while Colin played? (She was not there.)

errors.w: When I played, a man was stopping.
errors.r: I was playing when a man stopped.

support: Mostre a tradução (PT) após a 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Set the scene and introduce the event.
Two actions at the same time.

items.en: I was walking in the park when it started to rain.
While I was cooking, he was watching TV.
In the end, we all laughed.

pages.note: Choose the 4 starred expressions for your own stories; the others help you react and close.

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks e relacionar cada um à parte da história.
solo: Pergunte “Where does it go in a story?”.
Peça uma frase própria para cada chunk ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um chunk e usa em uma frase.
Duplas: contar uma história de 3 frases.
answers: Scene · two actions · surprise · more · ending
extra: Which of these would you use with a child?

errors.w: I was walking when it begins to rain.
errors.r: I was walking when it began to rain.

errors.w: Suddenly I was seeing a dog.

patterns.name: Background action
ex: We were walking in the park.
He was looking for a musician.

patterns.name: Interrupting action
ex: I was playing when a man stopped.
We were eating when the lights went out.
She was driving when the phone rang.

patterns.name: Two actions at once
ex: While I was playing, he recorded me.
While we were talking, it started to rain.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I was just walking and, bam, it rained.
I was walking when it began to rain.
So then he’s like, “Play it again.”
Then he asked me to play it again.
I did not understand what he said.
Long story short, he loved it.
In short, he was very pleased.
register.note: In informal storytelling you may hear “he’s like…”; in writing, use the full structure.

teach.goal: Past continuous = cena de fundo; past simple = evento. Foco em “was/were + -ing” e “when”.
solo: Mostre os padrões no diálogo.
Use “Swap the words” em voz alta.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
Duplas: um conta o fundo, o outro o evento.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03 é expansão.
extra: What were you doing when the teacher called you?
Tell me what you were doing at midnight yesterday.

errors.w: I played when he stopped. (ação interrompida)
errors.r: I was playing when he stopped.

errors.w: While I played, he was recorded.
errors.r: While I was playing, he recorded me.

support: Fique só com “I was… when…” na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine os três padrões em uma frase.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: “Was” and “were” are weak in connected speech: /wəz/ and /wɚ/. The strong word is the verb: “I was PLAYing”.

items.say: I was playing in the park.
items.linked: I wəz PLAY·ing in the PARK.

own.prompt: Write a sentence with “I was … when …” about something real.
own.criteria: Say it twice: slowly, then with weak “was”. Did the verb sound stronger than “was”?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: forma fraca de was/were e acento no verbo.
solo: Escutar e identificar → repetir → frase própria.
Bata palmas nas sílabas fortes.
group: Coro, depois duplas.
Cada estudante cria uma frase.
answers: Identify 1: I was playing. · Identify 2: While we were walking…

errors.w: Acentuar was em vez do verbo

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. Set the scene: you were reading in the park.
opts: I was reading in the park.
I was read in the park.

items.q: 2. A dog ran up while you were eating. Which is correct?
opts: I was eating when a dog ran up.
I ate when a dog was running up.
I was eat when a dog ran up.
items.why: Long action in the continuous, interruption in the past simple.

items.q: 4. A friend says “You won’t believe what happened!” You respond:
items.why: A natural reaction that invites the story.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: We ___ walking in the park when it started to rain.
___ I was playing, he recorded me.

ans: I was cooking when the phone rang.
I was cooking when my phone rang.
items.model: I was cooking when the phone rang.
items.from: I was cooking. The phone rang.

items.npc: I was walking home when I saw a rainbow.
items.why: Show interest and ask for more.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que justifique cada resposta.
Peça a história completa a partir de cada item.
group: Duplas comparam antes de revelar.
Pontos por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: I was reading in the park. · 2: I was eating when a dog ran up. · 3: Suddenly · 4: And then what happened?
Gap: were · While · I was playing my fiddle. · I was cooking when the phone rang. · Really? And then what happened?
extra: Say each answer with story intonation.

errors.w: I was eating when a dog was running.
errors.r: I was eating when a dog ran up.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — tell your story

brief.teacher: You are a curious friend. Ask “And then what happened?” and react with surprise.
brief.student: Tell a short true (or invented) story: set the scene, say what happened and how it ended.

orders: A funny moment on a trip
A day when everything went wrong
complications: You forget a word: describe it.
The friend says “Really? That happened to me too!”
You need to finish in 30 seconds.
success: I react to my partner’s story.

teach.goal: Contar uma história pessoal com começo, surpresa e fim.
solo: Use uma história real do aluno.
Rodada 1 com chunks, 2 palavras-chave, 3 livre.
Anote 2–3 correções.
extra: What was the last funny thing that happened to you?
What was your best day ever?

errors.w: Yesterday I was go to the market and I seen…
errors.r: Yesterday I went to the market and I saw…

stretch: Conte a história de forma mais curta e mais dramática.

b.title: Student B: witness notes
b.task: You know Mia at 8:00 and Tom at 9:00. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência em perguntas e respostas no passado contínuo.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥2 perguntas What was… doing?
Sem salas simultâneas.
answers: Info gap: A tem Tom 8:00 e Mia 9:00; B tem Mia 8:00 e Tom 9:00. Respostas com “was … -ing”.
extra: What was Tom doing at 9:00?

pages.title: Group mission — tell a story together
pages.goal: Each group must build and tell a short story with scene, surprise and ending.

missions.mission: Create a story with five sentences: one person starts, each adds one sentence.
Interview a classmate about a strange thing that happened to them. Ask follow-up questions.
Find out who broke a vase: ask what each person was doing at 7 p.m.

teach.goal: Construir uma história coletiva usando passado contínuo e simples.
group: Cada grupo recebe papéis e restrição.
Progressão: com chunks, palavras-chave, sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
answers: Modelo: “I was walking when I saw a big dog.” → “And then what happened?” → “Suddenly it ran to me. In the end, it was friendly.”
extra: Which story was funniest?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short story (4–5 sentences) about a surprising moment: scene, surprise and ending.
pages.model: Last Sunday I was walking in the park when I heard music. While I was listening, a man asked me to play with him. Suddenly, everyone was clapping! In the end, I made a new friend.
checklist: I closed with In the end.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points and show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta: uma história com estrutura.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários.
group: Troquem os textos e leiam em voz alta.
extra: Add a surprising ending.

errors.w: I was walking when I hear music.
errors.r: I was walking when I heard music.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Add follow-up questions and longer answers.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You told the story in order and used “when” and “while”.
prompts.improve: Example: Use weak “was” and stress the verb.
prompts.next: Example: Tell a two-minute story without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais. Foco desta aula: estrutura da história e passado contínuo.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você comenta.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.prompt: Add a surprise to your story with a word.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio telling a short story.
Write a 5-sentence story with when, while and suddenly.

Listen to the dialogue again and find two reactions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem anotações: cena, reação e surpresa.
group: Exit challenge individual.
answers: I was cooking when the phone rang. · Really? And then what happened? · Suddenly, it started to rain.
extra: Revisão espaçada: próxima aula, uma semana depois e na missão da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The situation stays the same; the language grows in length, nuance and autonomy.

ladder.goal: Tell a story in very short phrases.

ladder.say: I was walking when it started to rain. Then I ran home.
ladder.goal: Tell a short story with when and then.

ladder.say: While I was walking home, it suddenly started to pour, so I ran into a café.
ladder.goal: Link events with while and suddenly.

ladder.say: I had just left work when the sky opened up, so I ducked into a café, soaked.
No sooner had I stepped outside than the heavens opened, which, frankly, felt like the perfect end to the day.
I’d barely reached the corner when the rain came down, as if the day itself had been waiting to make its point.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está (A2) e a próxima etapa (B1).
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
